pr_title: [WIP] Don't schedule unnecessary output frames, and simplify damage functions
pr_body:
The `whole` argument has been removed from `damage_surface_iterator` because it was never used. As this function now only deals with partial damaging, it's been changed to return early if there is no damage and avoids scheduling a frame unnecessarily.

With the removal of the `whole` argument, `output_damage_from_view` just called `output_damage_view` with the same arguments, so I've combined these into the one function and renamed it to `output_damage_view_surfaces`.

Lastly, `output_damage_whole_container_iterator` is now removed as it was never used. `output_damage_whole_container` just damages the container including decorations and doesn't care about surfaces.

Probably closes #2748, but I'd like to see before and after metrics...
pr_comments:
>The whole argument has been removed from damage_surface_iterator because it was never used

What happens if you map a view with popups/subsurfaces outside the window geometry?

`handle_commit` calls `view_damage_from`, which iterates each output and calls `output_damage_view_surfaces`. That calls `output_view_for_each_surface`, therefore calling `damage_surface_iterator` with each surface. It works the same way as it did before.

>therefore calling damage_surface_iterator with each surface

I mean, it should damage the whole surfaces, it shouldn't take the damage from the surfaces. So we need `whole`.

issue_context.title: sway wasting significant CPU on clients that don't refresh often
issue_context.body:
To reproduce: play any audio file with embedded artwork in mpv with the wayland backend
Result: sway wastes 60% CPU while mpv wastes 10% more than it needs to

What happens is that with embedded artwork, mpv doesn't have anything to draw hence reschedules the frame callback to the next opportunity using wl_surface_commit() without damaging anything.
sway seems to do a lot of spinlocking and locking in general as seen on perf. At least it doesn't damage the whole surface.
comments: What perf arguments are you using?

Just perf top, but mostly looked at htop.
The PR as-is does fix the issue, now mpv spends as much time as it needs to decode the audio and sway's CPU use is the same as in idle with just htop open (0.0% - 1.3%).

review_comments: Not sure this is correct. We should still send `frame` events to surfaces that registered a frame callback even if there's no damage.
(Note: not sending frame callbacks when the view isn't damaged has caused bugs with mpv in the past)
